incident-bot: Paging: Canary rollout for release/edge-optimizer v3.2.1 is triggering elevated 5xx and tail latency on canary pool. Alert: 3.4% 5xx over last 5m, p99 latency +250ms. Impact: some hosted API customers are seeing failed generations. Runbook suggests immediate kill-switch + rollback. Assigned: @Alice Nguyen (oncall-sre), @Ben Carter (eng-platform). https://internal/runbooks/rollback-canary

Alice Nguyen: saw it on dashboards, yep — spiking errors correlated with canary hosts. Confirming which flag controls canary traffic.

Ben Carter: flag is feature.edge_optimizer_canary (fabric). We can flip to `off` to force traffic back to stable and then trigger automated rollback.

Maya Patel: paging from support — several customers reported timeouts in the last 10m. I've opened a ticket and am triaging.

Rajiv Kumar: quick ask: do we need db/schema changes? or is this pure inference path?

Alice Nguyen: pure inference. No migrations. Priority is stop the canary traffic. I'll run the kill-switch now.

Alice Nguyen: running:
```
# feature flag flip
redwoodctl feature set feature.edge_optimizer_canary false --env hosted --actor alice
```

Alice Nguyen: flag flipped to false. Waiting for traffic shift. Adding traffic-drain on canary nodes as a belt-and-suspenders:
```
kubectl label nodes canary=true && kubectl cordon <canary-node> && kubectl drain <canary-node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

Ben Carter: good. Also triggering a controlled undo on the canary deployment:
```
redwoodctl rollout undo --deployment edge-optimizer --namespace prod-canary --to-revision stable
```

incident-bot: Action log: feature.flag.updated by alice; rollout.undo initiated by ben.

Olivia Chen: I've kicked off smoke tests against stable (first 10 requests). Will paste results in a sec.

Olivia Chen: smoke results:
- /health: 200 OK
- sample generation (prompt id 42): returned in 120ms, no 5xx

Maya Patel: CS update: notified affected customers (ticket #5421, #5423, #5429). Mentioned we're rolling back canary and monitoring. No P0 escalations yet but they're watching.

Rajiv Kumar: metrics look promising — 5xx down from 3.4% -> 0.3% over 4m since flag flip. p99 latency trending down.

Alice Nguyen: monitoring graphs show error budget recovering. I'll keep the canary nodes cordoned until we validate for 15m.

Ben Carter: adding a postmortem stub: linking to incident doc and capturing hypothesis: regression in attention kernel path for sequence lengths >1024 causing OOMs and 5xx. We'll rollback model variant and run deeper repro.

Olivia Chen: running a small regression test on a local repro with the canary model; will post logs if it reproduces.

support-bot: Notifying support channel and creating post-incident escalation doc: https://internal/support/incidents/5421

Maya Patel: customer impact summary for ops: ~7 hosted customers experienced elevated error rates, median duration ~12m, peak impacted requests ~1200 per minute across the canary pool. No data exfiltration.

Alice Nguyen: manual verification: ran 30 sample generations across regions eu-west/us-east/ap-south — all green.

incident-bot: Canary rollback complete. Traffic shifted away from canary. Auto-alerts suppressed.

Ben Carter: next steps: schedule a canary hold, disable auto-rollout for v3.2.1 until root cause fix. I'll open an RFC for kernel fallback.

Rajiv Kumar: agree. We should add a smoke gating check for sequence length distribution in canary e2e before auto-promotion.

Maya Patel: CS notified customers with a brief summary and ETA for a root-cause update. No credits yet; will escalate if they ask.

Alice Nguyen: handing off to night oncall @Ben for post-rollback watch. I'll remain in the channel for 15m then depart.

Ben Carter: taking handoff. I'll keep monitors at 1min and will escalate if error >0.5% sustained for 5m.

Olivia Chen: saving logs and attaching minimal repro to the ticket.

incident-bot: Timeline summary appended to incident doc. Closing thread when all action items assigned.

Alice Nguyen: thanks all — great coordination. :tada:

Ben Carter: closing the loop: monitors stable at 30m post rollback, handover to eng-platform for root cause.

Maya Patel: support will follow up with customers tomorrow with RCA.

Alice Nguyen: leaving channel (oncall handoff complete).
